definitions.explanation: A small shelf or miniature shrine installed high on a wall in Japanese homes and businesses to enshrine Shinto talismans ({御札|おふだ}). Used for daily prayers and offerings to the kami.

examples.japanese: {毎朝|まいあさ}{神棚|かみだな}に{手|て}を{合|あ}わせる。
examples.english: I put my hands together in prayer at the kami shelf every morning.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{御札|おふだ}を{神棚|かみだな}に{祀|まつ}った。
examples.english: I enshrined a new talisman on the kami shelf.

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}の{家|いえ}には{立派|りっぱ}な{神棚|かみだな}があり、{毎日|まいにち}{水|みず}と{米|こめ}を{供|そな}えていた。
examples.english: My grandfather's house had an impressive kami shelf, and he would offer water and rice there every day.

notes:
USAGE:
A compound of {神|かみ} (god, kami) and {棚|たな} (shelf). Traditionally placed high on a wall in the living room or a prominent room. The Buddhist equivalent is {仏壇|ぶつだん} (Buddhist altar). Some households have both.

Offerings typically include {米|こめ} (rice), {水|みず} (water), {塩|しお} (salt), and {榊|さかき} (sakaki branches).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {神棚|かみだな}に{祀|まつ}る: to enshrine on the kami shelf
- {神棚|かみだな}に{手|て}を{合|あ}わせる: to pray at the kami shelf
- {神棚|かみだな}に{供|そな}える: to make offerings at the kami shelf
- {神棚|かみだな}を{設|もう}ける: to set up a kami shelf
